approaches.title: Selection sort — place the next minimum
approaches.explanation: For every position, find the smallest value in the remaining suffix and swap it into place.

approaches.title: Bubble sort — early-exit adjacent swaps
approaches.explanation: Bubble the largest unsorted value to the end. Stop when an entire pass makes no swap.

approaches.title: Insertion sort — grow a sorted prefix
approaches.explanation: Insert each element into its correct place in the sorted prefix by shifting larger values right.

approaches.title: Single pass — track the running maximum
approaches.explanation: Every element is inspected once; keep only the largest value seen so far.

approaches.title: Single pass — maintain largest and second largest
approaches.explanation: Update the second largest only when a value falls strictly between the two tracked values.

approaches.title: Top-down merge sort — divide and merge
approaches.explanation: Split until each range has one element, then merge two sorted halves with one temporary buffer.

approaches.title: Quick sort — Lomuto partition
approaches.explanation: Partition around a pivot so smaller values move left and larger values move right, then sort both sides.

approaches.title: Two pointers — compact unique values
approaches.explanation: Because the array is sorted, write each new value immediately after the last distinct value.

approaches.title: 3D dynamic programming — synchronize two robots
approaches.explanation: Track both robot columns on each row. Try all nine pairs of next moves and count a cell once when both robots occupy it.

approaches.title: BFS by level + parent map — enumerate shortest paths
approaches.explanation: A level-aware BFS records every predecessor that reaches a word at its shortest distance. Backtracking from the target reconstructs all shortest ladders.

approaches.title: Memoized recursion over index and remaining sum
approaches.explanation: Try to take or skip each value and memoize the remaining target at every index — overlapping branches collapse into one lookup.

approaches.title: One-dimensional tabulation over reachable sums
approaches.explanation: Sweep values once and mark every reachable sum, iterating the sum dimension backwards so each value is used at most once.

approaches.title: Memoized recursion on half the total
approaches.explanation: An odd total can never split evenly. Otherwise ask whether some subset reaches exactly half the total, memoizing (index, remaining half).

approaches.title: Rolling boolean table to reach half the sum
approaches.explanation: The same reachable-sums table as subset sum, checked against half the total with a single boolean array.

approaches.title: Memoized recursion over the remaining amount
approaches.explanation: At every remaining amount try each coin and keep the minimum count; amounts that cannot be formed stay at infinity.

approaches.title: Bottom-up minimum coins per amount
approaches.explanation: Build answers amount by amount: dp[a] is the fewest coins that reach a, starting from dp[0] = 0.

approaches.title: Memoized combination count over coin index
approaches.explanation: Walk the coin list once: each coin is either skipped or taken again, which counts every unordered combination exactly once.

approaches.title: One-dimensional unordered combination DP
approaches.explanation: Coins in the outer loop and amounts increasing inner keeps every combination counted once in a fixed coin order — dp[a] += dp[a - coin].

approaches.title: Memoized take-or-skip with item reuse
approaches.explanation: Because an item may be used any number of times, the take branch keeps the same index and only reduces the capacity.

approaches.title: One-dimensional capacity sweep with forward loop
approaches.explanation: Sweep capacities upward so dp[c - wt] is already updated in this pass — a forward inner loop is exactly what makes each item reusable.

approaches.title: Memoized match-or-skip on two indices
approaches.explanation: Matching characters consume both indices and add one; otherwise drop a character from either string and keep the better branch.

approaches.title: Two rolling rows of the LCS table
approaches.explanation: Roll the classic table into previous and current rows — each cell needs only the diagonal and the two neighbours from the row before.

approaches.title: Length from the LCS table
approaches.explanation: The shortest common supersequence interleaves both strings, so its length is len(a) + len(b) minus the length of their LCS.

approaches.title: Backtrack the LCS table to build the string
approaches.explanation: Walk back through the table: a matching character is appended once, otherwise move from the side with the longer common subsequence and append its character.

approaches.title: Memoized suffix recursion with three operations
approaches.explanation: Equal characters move both pointers for free; otherwise pay one for insert, delete, or replace and memoize on the suffix pair.

approaches.title: Two-row edit distance table
approaches.explanation: The recurrence only reads the previous row, so two rolling arrays replace the full table.

approaches.title: Memoized wildcard matching
approaches.explanation: A star can match nothing (advance the pattern) or one more character (consume text); question marks and exact letters advance both.

approaches.title: Bottom-up wildcard table
approaches.explanation: Leading stars match the empty prefix, then each cell combines the row above for stars or the diagonal for a single-character match.

approaches.title: Quadratic DP over the ending index
approaches.explanation: dp[i] is the longest increasing subsequence that ends at i, extended from every earlier smaller element.

approaches.title: Patience sorting with binary search
approaches.explanation: Keep the smallest possible tail for each subsequence length; binary search where the current value extends or replaces a tail.

approaches.title: Memoized burst ordering on intervals
approaches.explanation: Think in reverse: pick which balloon bursts last in an interval — its neighbours are then the interval walls, so the two sides become independent.

approaches.title: Interval-length tabulation
approaches.explanation: Fill the same recurrence by increasing interval length so both sub-intervals are ready before the current one.

approaches.title: Memoized ways for the last one or two steps
approaches.explanation: The final step is reached either from n − 1 or n − 2, so the count is the sum of both — memoize each n once.

approaches.title: Two rolling values — Fibonacci in disguise
approaches.explanation: Only the previous two counts are ever needed, so two variables replace the whole table.

approaches.title: Memoized minimum energy from the last stone
approaches.explanation: Standing on stone i, the cheapest arrival is the better of coming from i − 1 or i − 2, plus the height gap paid.

approaches.title: Rolling the last two stone costs
approaches.explanation: Process stones left to right keeping only the costs of the previous two positions.

approaches.title: Memoized, trying all k previous stones
approaches.explanation: From stone i the frog may hop back to any of the previous k stones — take the cheapest jump and memoize the result.

approaches.title: Tabulated cost per stone with k-wide lookback
approaches.explanation: Fill dp left to right; dp[i] checks the previous k stones in one inner loop.

approaches.title: Memoized pick-or-skip over the last index
approaches.explanation: Either skip the last element or take it and jump two positions back — take whichever is larger.

approaches.title: Two rolling sums — skip or take
approaches.explanation: Keep the best sums up to the previous two positions and extend with either decision.

approaches.title: Memoized loot ending at each house
approaches.explanation: Robbing house i forces skipping i − 1, so compare robbing it with skipping it and memoize.

approaches.title: Two rolling values along the street
approaches.explanation: Same recurrence as non-adjacent sums, sweeping the street once with two variables.

approaches.title: Space-optimized sweep over days and last task
approaches.explanation: Keep the best points per last task for the previous day; each new day tries every task except the one just done.

approaches.title: One-dimensional grid DP
approaches.explanation: Every cell is reached from above or from the left, so dp[j] = dp[j] + dp[j − 1] over a single row array.

approaches.title: Combinatorics — choose the down moves
approaches.explanation: A path is exactly m − 1 downs placed among m + n − 2 total moves — compute C(m + n − 2, m − 1) with rolling multiplication and division.

approaches.title: Row sweep with obstacle resets
approaches.explanation: Reuse the 1-D DP; an obstacle zeroes its cell, everything else keeps the from-above plus from-left sum.

approaches.title: Row-by-row DP over the three neighbours
approaches.explanation: For every cell take the cheapest of the three cells above it and add its own value.

approaches.title: Bottom-up triangle reduction in place
approaches.explanation: Start from the last row and fold upward: each cell takes itself plus the smaller of its two children.

approaches.title: Reachable-sums table, then closest to half
approaches.explanation: Mark every reachable subset sum, then pick the sum closest to half the total — its gap is the minimum difference.

approaches.title: Counting DP with modulo, one row
approaches.explanation: dp[s] counts subsets reaching s; each value adds the ways that used it exactly once by iterating sums backwards.

approaches.title: Reduce to counting subsets of a target sum
approaches.explanation: If one part sums to x and the other to total − x, the difference is total − 2x — so count subsets summing to (total + diff) / 2.

approaches.title: Signed sum becomes a subset-count
approaches.explanation: Splitting nums into plus and minus parts, a target needs the plus part to sum to (total − target) / 2 — count those subsets.

approaches.title: Best price per length — unbounded knapsack
approaches.explanation: dp[len] takes the best of every first cut, reusing the already-solved remainder — pieces may repeat, so no backwards trick needed.

approaches.title: Build the table, then backtrack the match
approaches.explanation: Fill the LCS table, then walk from the bottom-right: equal characters join the answer, otherwise step toward the larger neighbour.

approaches.title: Common-suffix lengths with rolling rows
approaches.explanation: dp[i][j] counts the common suffix ending at both characters — it resets to zero on a mismatch, so track the maximum.

approaches.title: Longest palindromic subsequence via LCS with the reverse
approaches.explanation: A palindromic subsequence read backwards appears in the reversed string too, so the answer is LCS(s, reverse(s)).

approaches.title: Characters left unmatched by the palindrome
approaches.explanation: Every character outside the longest palindromic subsequence needs one insertion — answer = n − LPS.

approaches.title: Keep the LCS, delete and insert the rest
approaches.explanation: Characters in the LCS stay untouched; the rest of A is deleted and the rest of B inserted — (n − lcs) + (m − lcs).

approaches.title: One row of distinct-subsequence counts
approaches.explanation: dp[j] counts ways to build t's prefix from s's prefix; iterating j backwards keeps the previous row's value for the diagonal.

approaches.title: One pass tracking the cheapest price so far
approaches.explanation: Sell only once, so the best sale at each day uses the minimum price seen before it.

approaches.title: Greedy — collect every upward slope
approaches.explanation: Unlimited transactions turn the answer into the sum of all positive day-to-day increases.

approaches.title: Four state variables for two transactions
approaches.explanation: Track the best balance after each of buy 1, sell 1, buy 2, sell 2 — each state extends the previous one day by day.

approaches.title: Generalized k-transaction DP
approaches.explanation: buy[t] and sell[t] hold the best balances with t transactions so far; when k is large enough every rise can be taken greedily.

approaches.title: Hold, sold, and rest states
approaches.explanation: A day after selling must be a rest day, so buying is only allowed from the rest state — three variables model it exactly.

approaches.title: Cash and hold states with a fee per sale
approaches.explanation: Two states suffice: cash (no stock) and hold (owning stock); selling pays the fee once.

approaches.title: Track parents while growing dp, then rebuild
approaches.explanation: Store which earlier index extended each dp entry, remember the endpoint of the best run, then walk parent pointers backwards.

approaches.title: Patience sorting — smallest tail per length
approaches.explanation: Keep the minimal possible tail for every subsequence length; binary search decides whether the current value extends a tail or replaces one.

approaches.title: Sort, then chain exactly like the LIS
approaches.explanation: After sorting, any valid subset is a chain where each element divides the next; dp plus parent pointers rebuild one longest chain.

approaches.title: Sort by length, extend chains with predecessors
approaches.explanation: A predecessor is one character shorter and a subsequence — check every shorter word pair after sorting by length.

approaches.title: Increasing and decreasing sweeps meet at a peak
approaches.explanation: Compute the longest increasing run ending at each index and the longest decreasing run starting there — the best peak combines both minus one.

approaches.title: Track counts alongside every length
approaches.explanation: Besides dp[i], keep count[i] — the number of longest runs ending at i; equal extensions add counts, longer ones replace them.

approaches.title: Memoized interval splitting
approaches.explanation: Split the matrix chain at every possible point k; the cost is left chain + right chain + the multiplication joining them.

approaches.title: Interval-length tabulation
approaches.explanation: Fill intervals by increasing length so both halves of every split are already computed.

approaches.title: Memoized cuts on the sorted stick
approaches.explanation: Sort the cuts and add virtual ends 0 and n; the first cut in a segment costs the segment length plus solving both sides.

approaches.title: Memoized truth counts on (i, j, want)
approaches.explanation: Each operator splits the expression into a left and right part; combine their true/false counts per operator truth table and memoize on (i, j, want).

approaches.title: Front partition — cut only at palindromic prefixes
approaches.explanation: Try every prefix that is a palindrome, pay one cut, and recurse on the rest; memoizing the starting index makes it fast enough for most inputs.

approaches.title: Palindrome table + minimum-cuts DP
approaches.explanation: Precompute pal[i][j] bottom-up, and cuts[i] = 0 if the whole suffix is a palindrome, otherwise one cut plus the best break after it.

approaches.title: Front partition with memo
approaches.explanation: Take the next subarray of length 1..k, it contributes its maximum times its length, and recurse from the next index.

approaches.title: Tabulated from the right
approaches.explanation: dp[i] is the best answer for the suffix starting at i; filling right to left needs nothing beyond dp itself.

approaches.title: Row-by-row histograms with a monotonic stack
approaches.explanation: Each row builds a running histogram of consecutive ones above it; the largest rectangle in that histogram is solved in linear time with a stack.

approaches.title: dp counts squares ending at each cell
approaches.explanation: If a cell is 1, the number of squares ending there is 1 plus the minimum of its top, left and diagonal neighbors — sum them all.

approaches.title: Sort both and match the smallest fitting cookie
approaches.time: O(n log n + m log m)
approaches.explanation: Give the least greedy child the smallest cookie that satisfies them; if it does not fit, the cookie is wasted on nobody.

approaches.title: BFS over adjacency lists, count starts
approaches.explanation: Build the adjacency list, then every unvisited node starts a BFS that marks its whole component; the number of starts is the answer.

approaches.title: Recursive DFS printing discovery order
approaches.explanation: Visit the start, record it, then recurse into every unvisited neighbor — the recursion stack is the DFS.

approaches.title: BFS over the adjacency matrix
approaches.explanation: isConnected[i][j] = 1 means a direct edge; every unvisited row starts a BFS that swallows its whole province.

approaches.title: Multi-source BFS from every 1 at once
approaches.explanation: Seed the queue with all cells holding 1, keep -1 as 'unknown distance', and let BFS fill distances layer by layer.

approaches.title: Multi-source BFS, one layer per minute
approaches.explanation: All rotten cells enter the queue together; each BFS layer is one minute, and the count of fresh cells tells whether it ever finishes.

approaches.title: DFS recolor guarded by the old color
approaches.explanation: Remember the starting color; recolor each cell outside in, stopping at walls, borders and already-recolored cells.

approaches.title: BFS carrying the parent of each node
approaches.explanation: A visited neighbor that is not our own parent proves a cycle — in an undirected graph that edge closes a loop.

approaches.title: DFS with a parent check
approaches.explanation: Recurse from each unvisited node; if a neighbor is visited and is not the parent we came from, the graph has a cycle.

approaches.title: DFS sinking each island
approaches.explanation: Every unvisited land cell triggers a DFS that sinks the entire island to water, so it can never be counted twice.

approaches.title: Two-color painting with DFS
approaches.explanation: Paint every node 0 or 1; a neighbor that already carries our color proves the graph cannot be split in two.

approaches.title: Three-state DFS — visiting vs finished
approaches.explanation: State 1 means the node is on the current recursion stack; reaching it again means the edge closes a directed cycle.

approaches.title: Post-order DFS pushed onto a stack
approaches.explanation: A node finishes only after all its descendants, so pushing nodes when their DFS ends and popping gives a valid topological order.

approaches.title: Kahn's algorithm — peel zero indegrees
approaches.explanation: Start from nodes nothing points to; removing a node frees its neighbors, and anyone whose indegree hits zero joins the order.

approaches.title: Kahn's count exposes the cycle
approaches.explanation: If some nodes never reach indegree zero, they sit on a cycle — the processed count tells you instantly.

approaches.title: Prerequisites as a DAG — finish iff no cycle
approaches.explanation: Draw b → a for every prerequisite pair and run Kahn's algorithm; finishing every course means the graph is acyclic.

approaches.title: Record the Kahn order, empty on a cycle
approaches.explanation: The same peeling process yields the actual study order; if fewer than n courses come out, no valid order exists.

approaches.title: Reverse edges and peel from terminal nodes
approaches.explanation: Terminal nodes are safe; a node becomes safe once all its outgoing edges lead to safe nodes — peel them off the reversed graph.

approaches.title: First differing characters give the edges
approaches.explanation: For each adjacent word pair, the first mismatch orders two letters; a topological sort of these 26 letters spells the alphabet.

approaches.title: BFS replacing one letter at a time
approaches.explanation: Every word is a node and a one-letter change is an edge; deleting words from the dictionary as you enqueue them keeps each visited once.

approaches.title: Plain BFS fills distances
approaches.explanation: With every edge of weight 1, BFS discovers nodes in non-decreasing distance so the first arrival is the shortest.

approaches.title: Topological order, then one relaxation pass
approaches.explanation: In a DAG every edge points forward in topological order, so a single sweep relaxes all distances without repeats.

approaches.title: Dijkstra with a priority queue
approaches.explanation: Always settle the closest unsettled node; stale entries with a bigger recorded distance are skipped.

approaches.title: Dijkstra without a priority queue — the O(V²) scan
approaches.explanation: Without a heap you rescan all nodes to find the next minimum each round; the priority queue turns exactly that step into O(log V).

approaches.title: BFS counting steps through open cells
approaches.explanation: Every move costs 1 on the grid, so BFS from the source reaches the destination in the fewest steps, avoiding walls and the border.

approaches.title: Dijkstra where the cost is the maximum jump
approaches.explanation: Keep the best achievable effort per cell; a move's effort is the max of the path so far and this step's height difference.

approaches.title: Layer-by-layer relaxation, one flight per stop
approaches.explanation: Relax all edges k+1 times, but keep the previous layer's distances intact so a path may use at most one extra flight per round.

approaches.title: Dijkstra, then the largest shortest distance
approaches.explanation: The signal reaches everyone at the slowest shortest path; if any node stays unreachable the answer is -1.

approaches.title: Count ways while Dijkstra tightens distances
approaches.explanation: A strictly shorter path resets the count to the predecessor's ways; an equal-length path adds them, all modulo 1e9+7.

approaches.title: BFS over the 0..99999 value space
approaches.explanation: Each multiplication is one step, so BFS over reachable products modulo 100000 finds the fewest operations; the first hit on end wins.

approaches.title: One adjacency list, then BFS and DFS orders
approaches.explanation: Build the graph once and show both traversals: BFS via a queue, DFS via recursion, from the same source.

approaches.title: Flood over 8-directional neighbors
approaches.explanation: Every 1 starts a component; the flood clears all ones connected to it, including diagonals.

approaches.title: Mark border-connected O's, then flip
approaches.explanation: Any O touching the border survives; mark all of those first, then everything left over is captured.

approaches.title: Flood from the border, count what remains
approaches.explanation: Land reachable from the edge can walk out; clear all of it, and the ones left behind are the enclaves.

approaches.title: Relax every edge n-1 times, then probe once more
approaches.explanation: After n-1 relaxing rounds all shortest paths settle; one extra round that still improves distances proves a negative cycle.

approaches.title: All pairs through every intermediate k
approaches.explanation: Try every vertex as an intermediate stop; -1 entries become a big sentinel so unreachable stays unreachable.

approaches.title: Floyd-Warshall, then count reachable neighbors
approaches.explanation: Compute all-pairs distances, count how many cities sit within the threshold of each one, and prefer the largest index on ties.

approaches.title: Prim's — grow the tree with the lightest frontier edge
approaches.explanation: A priority queue holds edges leaving the tree; always take the cheapest edge to a node outside and add its weight.

approaches.title: Union-Find with path compression and rank
approaches.explanation: find flattens the path to the root; union attaches the smaller rank tree under the bigger one, keeping operations near constant.

approaches.title: Kruskal's — sort edges, union what is still apart
approaches.explanation: Process edges from cheapest to priciest; take one only when it links two different components, stopping after n-1 edges.

approaches.title: Components minus one after proving enough edges
approaches.explanation: Fewer than n-1 cables can never connect n machines; otherwise each union merges two groups and the answer is groups-1.

approaches.title: Union row and column ids, count the groups
approaches.explanation: Each stone glues its row and column together; within one group of size s you can remove s-1 stones, so answer = stones - groups.

approaches.title: Share an email, share a person
approaches.explanation: Whenever an email appears under another account, union the two accounts; then group emails by root and attach the owner name.

approaches.title: Add land, union with wet neighbors
approaches.explanation: Each operation plants one cell, raising the count by one, then every already-planted neighbor union merges two islands back into one.

approaches.title: Union existing islands, then test every flip
approaches.explanation: First union all adjacent land with size tracking; flipping a water cell merges up to four distinct neighboring islands, so try each cell.

approaches.title: Dijkstra where time is the worst cell on the path
approaches.explanation: Track the earliest time each cell becomes reachable — the max elevation along the path; a priority queue always expands the easiest frontier.

approaches.title: Tarjan's tin/low — the edge no cycle can bypass
approaches.explanation: An edge to a child is a bridge when the child's low value stays above our tin — nothing below climbs back to us or higher.

approaches.title: Articulation points — root child count and low checks
approaches.explanation: A node is critical when a child's low reaches at least its tin; the DFS root is special and needs two or more children.

approaches.title: Kosaraju — finish order, flip the graph, count
approaches.explanation: Take nodes in DFS finishing order, then flood the reversed graph from each unvisited one; every flood is exactly one SCC.

approaches.title: One pass comparing neighbors
approaches.explanation: The array is sorted when no element is smaller than the one before it.

approaches.title: Save the first, shift everything left
approaches.explanation: Stash arr[0], slide each element one slot left, then drop the stashed value at the end.

approaches.title: Reverse three times instead of shifting k times
approaches.explanation: Reverse the first k, reverse the rest, then reverse the whole array — the two blocks trade places in place.

approaches.title: Compact non-zeroes, fill the tail with zeros
approaches.explanation: Write every non-zero at the next free slot keeping order; whatever space remains becomes zero.

approaches.title: Check every element in order
approaches.explanation: No ordering guarantees, so the only option is to scan until the value shows up or the array ends.

approaches.title: Two pointers, skipping duplicates
approaches.explanation: Walk both sorted arrays together; matches advance both pointers and only new values get appended.

approaches.title: XOR of 1..n against the array
approaches.explanation: Every present number cancels itself between the two XOR runs, leaving exactly the missing value.

approaches.title: Reset the run on every zero
approaches.explanation: Keep a current streak of ones and the best seen so far; a zero resets the streak.

approaches.title: XOR everything — pairs cancel
approaches.explanation: x ^ x = 0 and x ^ 0 = x, so every duplicated number wipes itself out and the loner remains.

approaches.title: Sliding window over positive values
approaches.explanation: With only positives the sum grows as the window extends, so shrink from the left whenever it overshoots k.

approaches.title: Prefix sums with first-seen indices
approaches.explanation: Negatives break the window, so remember the earliest index of every prefix sum; a match k apart gives the best length.

approaches.title: Remember what the complement needs
approaches.explanation: Scan once keeping value → index; if the current complement was seen earlier, that pair is the answer.

approaches.title: Dutch national flag — three pointers
approaches.explanation: 0s grow at the front, 2s at the back; mid walks the unknown zone and swaps decide where each value lands.

approaches.title: Boyer-Moore voting
approaches.explanation: Keep a candidate and a balance; different values cancel the balance, and a majority survives every cancellation.

approaches.title: Kadane — extend or restart
approaches.explanation: At each index decide whether the best subarray ending here extends the previous one or starts fresh; keep the running maximum.

approaches.title: Kadane tracking the window boundaries
approaches.explanation: Whenever a fresh start beats extending, remember the new beginning; record start/end each time the best improves.

approaches.title: Track the cheapest price so far
approaches.explanation: Sell at today's price only against the minimum seen before today; the best of those trades is the answer.

approaches.title: Two write pointers, even for pos and odd for neg
approaches.explanation: Positives land at indexes 0, 2, 4... and negatives at 1, 3, 5..., preserving their relative order automatically.
